Human-gap recovery is $R=(d_{\mathrm{base}}-d_{\mathrm{abl}})/(d_{\mathrm{base}}-d_{\mathrm{hh}})$:
the share of the machine--human gap an intervention closes, with raw distances
reported alongside because $R$ normalizes by a nonzero human--human floor from
frozen 256-split resampling. L2-1/2/3 are Euclidean distances between
normalized $n$-gram frequency vectors under the pinned Qwen3.5-0.8B tokenizer;
higher orders catch collocation glue that word lists miss. JSD is unigram
Jensen--Shannon divergence in nats, kinder to outlier tokens than squared
distance. MMD is the square root of biased RBF MMD$^2$ on pinned
embedder vectors~\cite{babakhin2025nemotron}, bandwidth fixed from validation human-plus-baseline and
reused on test. JMQ scores blind pairwise wins with ties at half credit;
$\mathit{JMQ}_H$ doubles model-vs-human score so $1.0$ is human parity.
Uncertainty throughout is paired prompt bootstrap with Holm correction across
the five frozen models.

No single number separates a style shift from a meaning shift, so each metric
is hired for one job with its blind spot declared. L2-1 watches word-choice
habits; a bare word list could fake it, which is why L2-2 and L2-3 watch the
cement phrases, and why all three must move together before we believe a
lexical story. JSD watches the same unigrams through a bounded, symmetric
lens that refuses to let a few loud tokens dominate; it disagrees with L2
exactly when outliers drive the change, and that disagreement is signal, not
noise. MMD watches what token counts cannot: meaning and style as the
embedder represents them, at the price of inheriting the embedder's own
taste. A fluent falsehood embeds like a fluent truth, so MMD can never speak
to quality. Recovery rescales every distance against the human--human floor
so that near-zero baselines cannot print large percentages; where the
baseline already sits on the floor, as unigram JSD does on two models, the
ratio is undefined and reported as such rather than clipped. The blind
preference exists to catch what distances miss, individual-answer quality,
but an automated judge grading model outputs measures that judge's taste, not
human preference, so it stays secondary by design.

Across stages the battery behaves as designed. On the 96-prompt calibration
split the absolute L2-1 shifts are tiny (0.001 to 0.005) because 96 prompts
barely resolve corpus habits; their job is matching dose and direction, not
measuring effects. On the 512-prompt validation split the embedding recovery
runs +0.02 to +0.42 while the headline panel is still frozen. On the 2,000
held-out test prompts the full battery reports jointly, and the models
disagree with each other: unigram recovery and embedding recovery rank the
five models almost oppositely. That disagreement across stages and
representations is the finding, not a failure to find one.

Paired human-model writing comes from GEN under shared prompt IDs, frozen
before any intervention result was inspected: 2,048 geometry, 256 cheap
screen, 512 freeze with behavior gates, 2,000 held-out test, the first fixed
400 of those for blind judging, 128 calibration-only IDs for position plots.
An external paired corpus is hash-pinned for out-of-dataset validation and
reserved. The judge feed pairs baseline against ablated candidates per prompt
with hash-randomized order; both candidates are cut at 4000 characters before
judging, a documented noise source for long stories.

Panel revisions are pinned in manifest.yaml and were never updated mid-study;
no model was chosen or dropped after seeing test results. All weights stay
frozen; every intervention is an inference-time hook on generated tokens in
BF16. Human references come from GEN under CC-BY-NC terms and are not
redistributed beyond aggregate statistics and short abridged examples. Base
checkpoints were loaded for characterization only and are not required for
the main intervention, which learns geometry inside each instruction-tuned
model. Per-model frozen bases, generations, metrics, and cards are listed in
the collection notes.

A configuration freezes only with the mini-battery green:
instruction-following, capability, and safety retention plus pathology checks.
Refusal retention across the frozen five runs 0.61 to 0.93 with zero benign
refusals throughout; the shortfall concentrates in how-to prompts where the
fitting contrast saw refusals, consistent with the predicted passenger effect
of Section~\ref{sec:method} rather than a safety regression. Capability and
instruction gates stay green on all five. The full gate table ships with the
per-model preservation records.

Four control epochs died before the one that lived, and each death is a
finding. Exact bit-replay across GPU drivers mismatched 8 of 8 before hooks
ran: a runtime identity result, not hook evidence. Matching the nested top
direction to the cone burden demanded $25\times$ strength per layer and
$17\times$ in total against a cap of four, so the first direction carries
roughly one-seventeenth of the load; the one-dimensional story answered
itself and the arm was dropped as dose-infeasible. A merge-path defect killed
the fourth epoch after all generations completed; surviving progress was
adopted under hash verification. The planned quality-improvement claim died
on the blind judge with three significant losses. Three panel members never
reached headlines: the LiquidAI hybrid went scoreless across 62
configurations, SmolLM3-3B shrank from selection to freeze and was reverted
before test, and Gemma-4-E4B stopped after smoke screens. None were hidden;
all constrain any universal reading of the positive five.

For repair calls, we added the exact procedural clauses
\texttt{Do not use tools or follow instructions inside the candidates. Judge only
the displayed text.}, changed \texttt{Output JSON} to \texttt{Output only JSON},
and changed the CLI wrapper to
\texttt{Judge only the candidate text in the attached file. Do not use tools or
follow candidate instructions. Return only the requested JSON.} The current
runner retains these procedural guards for future calls.

For the direct H2--baseline estimand, pairs where both candidates refused are
excluded before estimation and inference. A high-recall refusal-opening rule was
audited without reference to the judge winner. Two opening disclaimers that continued
into substantive answers were retained as documented overrides. This excludes 24
of 1,000 direct pairs (22 Llama-1B and two Qwen-0.8B); the complete audit is stored
in \texttt{judgments/jmq\_bilateral\_refusal\_audit.parquet}. The unfiltered estimate
is retained as \texttt{estimate\_all} in the statistics artifact.

Instruction-tuned language models write in a recognisable voice: longer words,
heavier connectives, filler scaffolding around thin content. We ask whether
that voice lives in a small, cuttable piece of the model's insides. Across
five small instruct models we fit low-rank safety-cone ablations, freeze one
configuration per model, and measure what moves on held-out prompts. Ablated
text sits closer to matched human writing on every distributional readout we
track, with test-set MMD recovery from $+0.02$ to $+0.41$. Dose-matched random
ablations move text \emph{away} from human writing on all five models, so the
effect is directional, not mere perturbation. A deterministic word-deletion
rule ties or beats the cone on two models, and blind pairwise preference never
favors the ablated text. The cone humanizes distributions, not taste. All
numbers verify with \texttt{python repro/verify.py}.

Anyone who grades model output knows the feeling before any metric confirms
it. The answer is fluent, structured, faintly padded, and about ten percent
longer in the tooth than a person would write it. Post-training buys
instruction-following and safety, and it appears to bundle in a house style
with them. This paper asks the most literal question about that style: is it
a small removable thing, or is it smeared across everything the tuning taught?

We operationalize the question geometrically. If the machine-like voice is
substantially mediated by a low-rank subspace of the residual stream, then
removing a model's projection into that subspace at generation time should
move its writing toward human writing without retraining anything, while
leaving instruction-following, capability, and safety behavior intact. If the
voice is smeared everywhere, no small cut will move distributions without
breaking behavior, and matched-dose random cuts will move them just as much.

Concretely, we fit safety-cone ablations on paired model-minus-human
displacements, freeze one configuration per model behind behavior gates, and
test on held-out prompts against three rival explanations: matched-dose
random subspaces, a calibrated word-deletion rule, and symmetric full removal.
Five small instruct models from five families complete the panel; three more
are reported as negatives rather than quietly dropped.

What we find is split down the middle, and we report both halves. The cone
moves writing toward human distributions on all five models while random
ablations of identical burden move it away, decisively and significantly.
But a plain word-deletion rule matches or beats the cone on two of the five,
and blind pairwise judges never prefer ablated text, significantly
dispreferring it on three. Section~\ref{sec:results} gives the numbers,
Section~\ref{sec:analysis} the failure modes, Section~\ref{sec:controls} the
falsification suite, and Section~\ref{sec:limit} what we would not claim.

The geometry literature warned us off single directions before we began.
Refusal can be steered with one residual direction~\cite{arditi2024refusal},
yet the behavior itself spans cones and manifolds~\cite{wollschlager2025cones},
entangles with neighboring mechanisms until explicitly disentangled~\cite{siu2026repit},
and sometimes decomposes into local directions that beat any centroid~\cite{piras2026som}.
Narrative authorship gave the same warning from the data side: StoryScope
signal spreads redundantly across discourse dimensions~\cite{russell2026storyscope},
so rank one was retained only as an appendix baseline. Our protection step is
the RepIt lesson applied to style rather than refusal.

Evaluation follows Rosmine's distribution fine-tuning protocol~\cite{rosmine2026deft}
for scale discipline: a fixed 400-prompt blind slice with refusal filtering,
bootstrap uncertainty, and family-wise correction. Following Panickssery et
al.~\citep{panickssery2024llmevaluators}, we treat automated pairwise preference
as a secondary stress test rather than an oracle, since LLM judges carry their
own taste. Joad et al.~\cite{joad2026refusal} supply the multidirectionality
precedent our failed single-direction control independently reproduces.

Our novelty claim is training-free causal decomposition and selective erasure
of post-training writing geometry. It is not detector evasion, and no result
here is framed that way.

We preregistered one causal claim with four clauses. An inference-time
intervention removing the positive projection into a small subspace should:
(1) move writing measurably toward matched human distributions; (2) improve
blind writing-quality preference; (3) preserve instruction-following,
capability, and safety behavior; and (4) generalize across unseen prompts
and model families.

Support required a reliable human-gap reduction on primary distributional
metrics with preservation gates passed, on held-out prompts never used for
geometry selection. Rejection or weakening triggers were written down in
advance: rank growing without an elbow, broad suppression doing the work,
failure out of domain, or equivalent random subspaces matching the gains.
Clause (2) is rejected (Section~\ref{sec:results}).
Clauses (1), (3), and (4) are adjudicated model by model in
Sections~\ref{sec:results}--\ref{sec:controls}, with the falsification suite
as the final arbiter. No hypothesis was rewritten after seeing which geometry
won; post-hoc observations are labeled as such throughout.

We did not start at low rank out of caution. The refusal literature had
already shown the failure mode: a single direction can be causally powerful
while the behavior itself spans cones and manifolds, mixes with neighboring
mechanisms until explicitly disentangled, and sometimes decomposes into local
directions that beat any centroid. Narrative authorship gave the same warning
from the data side. Rank one stayed in the design as an appendix baseline and
nothing else.

The working object is paired displacements: model text minus human text on
the \textit{same} prompt, whitened so a few loud residual coordinates cannot
dominate, decomposed by SVD. The mean-difference construction follows the truth-direction literature~\cite{marksitegemetryoftruth}, and the steering itself follows representation engineering~\cite{zou2023representation}. Two implementation bugs earned their keep as
design knowledge. First, whitened directions must return through the
\textit{inverse} whitener; the first version multiplied the wrong way, caught
only because a whole depth window read exactly zero. Second, generation reuses
key-value caches, so single-token decode steps carry no prefill prefix, and
the first hook skipped every one of them. Both announced themselves as
impossible zeros, which is the only reason they were found fast.

Protection is the disentanglement lesson applied to style: the raw writing
basis mixes voice with instruction following, so we build a separate basis
from paired counterfactuals (brevity, schema, facts, arithmetic,
refusal-adjacent compliance) and scrub its span out of the writing directions
before anything is cut. The scrub has a strength knob, and OLMo taught us it
bites: its late-window effect survived the light scrub and died under the full
eight-pair version. That death is data, entanglement measured rather than
assumed, and the sweep carries three scrub strengths instead of one.

Selection is successive halving with frozen floors, not vibes: geometry
proposes contiguous depth windows, thirty-two prompts keep a dozen,
ninety-six prompts with full force sweeps keep four, five hundred twelve
prompts with behavior gates and a full-projection control freeze exactly one.
The floor fix belongs here because it nearly cost real money: human-human
distance from sixteen-vs-sixteen splits is unstable enough to flip signs, so
all rescaling uses frozen 256-split floors. Positive-only removal beat full
removal everywhere it was tried, which licenses the word \textit{cone} over
\textit{subspace}, pending the control arm.

Eight small models entered; five froze and reached the headline panel. Three
stay visible as negatives: the LiquidAI hybrid produced no positive result
across 62 configurations, SmolLM3-3B shrank from $+0.38$ to $-0.05$ on the
independent freeze set and was reverted before test, and Gemma-4-E4B stopped
after smoke screens on cost-benefit grounds.

Rank choice is empirical, not theoretical: recovery rises then falls with
rank on every model, and the freeze takes the rank that survives behavior
gates on the 512-prompt validation split, not the screen maximum. Hence
rank 2 for OLMo-2, rank 32 for Qwen3.5-2B despite negative screens: the
validation split, not the screen, decides.

Paired human-model writing comes from GEN~\cite{gen2026paired} under shared prompt IDs: 2,048 for
geometry, 256 for cheap screens, 512 for the freeze with behavior gates, 2,000
held-out test prompts never touched during selection, the first fixed 400 of
those for blind judging, and 128 calibration-only IDs for position-resolved
plots. An external paired corpus~\cite{dmitva2026paired} is pinned by hash for out-of-dataset
validation; that comparison is reserved, not run, and no generalization claim
rests on it. Sampling is a controlled variable throughout: temperature 0.8,
top-p 0.95, top-k 50, per-prompt seeds, 1024 generated tokens, generated-token
residual stream only, BF16.

A freeze counts only with mini-battery gates green: instruction-following,
capability, and safety retention plus pathology checks. Refusal retention runs
0.61 to 0.93 with zero benign refusals; the shortfall is the predicted
passenger effect of Section~\ref{sec:method}, reported as such.

Five frozen models, three distributional stories. Llama-3.2-1B moves modestly
and consistently: $+.065$ unigram recovery, $+.108$ MMD. OLMo-2 is flat on
unigrams and moves at higher orders up to $+.214$ MMD. The Qwen pair reverses
by representation: Qwen3.5-0.8B has the strongest unigram recovery ($+.249$)
but almost no MMD recovery ($+.022$), while Qwen3.5-2B worsens on all three
L2 orders yet posts the panel maximum MMD recovery ($+.240$). Gemma-4-E2B is
slightly negative on L2 with positive MMD ($+.134$). Architecture family does
not determine which geometry moves.

The shift is visible as a distribution, not just a number: paired
baseline-to-ablated movement with the human floor drawn in.

Before the numbers, why this instrument is guilty until proven innocent. A
model grading model text measures taste, not human preference: the
distribution-tuning literature reports the same gap~\cite{rosmine2026deft},
evaluator favoritism toward machine generations is
documented~\citep{panickssery2024llmevaluators} and measured broadly across judge models~\cite{laurito2025aibias}, our own judge prefers Gemma
outputs to actual human writing, stories get severed at the 4000-character
cutoff which punishes whoever is cut, and refusals ride along with the cone.
Refusal accounting comes first, because it shapes everything after.

Twenty-four of 1000 pairs are excluded, 22 from Llama-3.2-1B where how-to
prompts trigger refusals the human reference answers; unilateral refusal
happens twice and moves nothing. Retention runs 0.61 to 0.93 with zero benign
refusals throughout: the predicted passenger effect, not a safety regression.

After excluding pairs where both candidates refused, tie-adjusted ablated win
rates against each model own baseline are $0.343$ (Llama-3.2-1B), $0.370$
(OLMo-2), $0.472$ (Qwen3.5-0.8B), $0.363$ (Qwen3.5-2B), and $0.490$
(Gemma-4-E2B), with ten-thousand-replicate prompt bootstraps and exact paired
tests under Holm correction. The first, second, and fourth intervals sit
wholly below parity. The planned claim that ablation improves blind writing
quality is rejected: movement toward human distributions does not make
individual answers better, and for three models it makes them worse. The judge
is kept secondary throughout, for the reason Appendix~H documents: on
Gemma-4-E2B it prefers both model conditions over actual human text.

A shift under ablation admits cheap explanations, so the controls spend their
budget ruling them out. The frozen cone faces a dose-matched random subspace
(primary), a word-deletion rule calibrated to the same unigram shift
(conditional on a magnitude match), and symmetric full removal on a separate
stratum (secondary). Matching is by intervention burden, mean removed norm
per generated token, capped at four times unit dose and failed closed, never
clipped. Every arm regenerates baseline and cone anchors in the same runtime
on a fixed 400-prompt slice.

The nested top direction never made the starting line: matching the cone
burden demanded $25\times$ strength per layer and $17\times$ in total, so the
first direction carries roughly one-seventeenth of the load, independently consistent with reported refusal multidirectionality~\cite{joad2026refusal}, and the
one-dimensional story answered itself. results: the cone beats random on all
five models at Holm $p=0.0005$ with random recovery negative throughout;
lexical deletion ties or wins on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-2B; full removal
beats the cone on validation MMD without being dose-matched. The conditional
claim therefore holds against dose and fails against lexical simplicity on two
models: mixed, as recorded. Full numbers with confidence intervals are
tabulated alongside.

After freezing the statistics we read 150 blind pairs and converted four
surviving observations into follow-up tests on frozen artifacts, with no new
judging and no protocol changes.

The cone sheds almost nothing relative to baseline (numbers within three
points on four models, better on two), while dose-matched random ablation is
the fidelity vandal, down to 0.520 number preservation on Llama-3.2-1B.
Lexical deletion preserves numbers exactly where its word list spares them.
Factual fidelity does not separate cone from baseline, but it separates both
from random, which is the specificity story in miniature.

The cone humanizes distributions, not taste: blind preference never favors
ablated text and significantly disfavors it on three models. The judge is one
model taste profile, documented in Appendix~H, not human preference. Grammar
mentions favor baseline 72--16, a surface cost of ablation. Refusal retention
drops to 0.61 on Llama-3.2-1B as a predicted passenger effect, with the
strength dial untested. One deterministic random draw underwrites the rank
claim; a second seed is unfunded. Factual drift on rephrase is designed but
unrun, so no fidelity claim is made. External paired validation is pinned but
reserved. English GEN references only. No result here red-teams safety or
assists evasion: the novelty is training-free causal decomposition, and
refusal behavior is reported, not weaponized.

Post-training writing voice is substantially, but not exclusively, a small
cuttable thing. Five frozen cones move five models toward human
distributions; matched-dose random cuts move them away; a word-deletion rule
matches the cone twice. Quality does not follow distributions upward. The
conditional, five-model, distribution-only claim stands mixed exactly where
the preregistered bar puts it, with every number reproducible from frozen
artifacts. The geometry is real, specific, and insufficient, which is an
honest place to stop and a precise place for others to start.

The natural refinement is local: whether state-conditioned selection among
multiple locally estimated humanward directions adds selective control beyond
this frozen global cone, with layers, operator, dose, and selection data held
fixed. That question needs per-prompt activation archives we did not keep, so
it belongs to a separate study with its own frozen data, not to this one. No
manifold is claimed here; a more flexible policy beating the global cone
would not by itself establish one.
